papers.title: Tau-driven hyperexcitability of locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons underlies sleep fragmentation and cognitive decline in mice.
papers.summary: Using P301S mice and cell-type-specific tau overexpression, the authors show that pathological tau selectively increases intrinsic excitability of locus coeruleus noradrenergic (LCDBH) neurons, producing sleep fragmentation, reduced NREM sleep and slow-wave activity, and recognition memory deficits. Optogenetic suppression of LCDBH-tau neuronal activity reversed sleep disturbances and rescued cognitive dysfunction.

papers.title: Disrupted sleep-wake regulation in the MCI-Park mouse model of Parkinson's Disease
papers.summary: The study characterized sleep-wake regulation in the MCI-Park mouse model of Parkinson's disease near the transition to the parkinsonian state, finding increased wakefulness, reduced NREM and REM sleep, greater sleep fragmentation, and altered EEG activity patterns that mirror those seen in PD patients. The authors propose the model as a tool to dissect circuit mechanisms of PD-associated sleep disruption and identify therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Thalamic stereo-EEG detects sleep stages N2 and N3 with discrimination approaching scalp EEG
papers.summary: Analyzed 477 h of simultaneous stereo-EEG and scalp EEG from six adults to test whether thalamic channels identify sleep stages N2+N3. Thalamic channels achieved AUCs of 0.94 (RF+HMM) and 0.93 (SleepSEEG) and outperformed mesial temporal and temporal neocortical channels in all six participants.

papers.title: Adapting Sleep Foundation Models for Dense Sleep Spindle Localization
papers.summary: Adapts a frozen SleepFM encoder with a local time-frequency pathway and residual cross-attention for dense sleep spindle localization, achieving event-level F1 of 0.8080±0.0040 at IoU 0.2 across six MODA folds. Ablations indicate localization depends mainly on local spectral and sub-token temporal information, with pretrained representation providing complementary context.

papers.title: Glial Control of Insomnia: Astrocyte-Microglia Interactions in Stress, Hyperarousal and Sleep Dysregulation.
papers.summary: Reviews clinical, experimental and translational evidence that astrocytes and microglia integrate stress signaling, neuroinflammation, synaptic plasticity and sleep homeostasis, proposing a coordinated stress-glia-insomnia axis. Highlights astrocyte-microglia crosstalk mechanisms such as purinergic signaling and calcium-dependent network synchronization as stabilizers of pathological hyperarousal, and discusses glia-targeted therapies.

papers.title: Anti-correlation time-frequency synergy and dual-granularity fusion for sleep stage classification.
papers.summary: Designs a single-channel EEG sleep staging network using anti-correlated multi-branch frequency features, dual-granularity residual attention fusion, causal transition-aware learning, and focal loss. It reached overall accuracies of 87.0%, 83.4%, and 84.5% on SleepEDF-20, SleepEDF-78, and SHHS, with N1 accuracies of 57.5%, 52.5%, and 49.3%.

papers.title: Effects of environmental enrichment and social isolation in preclinical rodent models: role of the endocannabinoid system.
papers.summary: Reviews preclinical rodent studies on environmental enrichment and social isolation, reporting that enrichment is most commonly associated with increased CB1 receptor expression while isolation is linked to disrupted CB1 receptor functionality and dysregulated endocannabinoid signaling. Effects are region-specific and modulated by manipulation type, duration, developmental stage, pathology and possibly sex.

papers.title: Physiological Sleep Features Associated With Dimensions of Daily Dysfunction in Insomnia.
papers.summary: Used exploratory factor analysis in 859 SAGIC adults (368 with insomnia) and found a single factor underlying nine daily dysfunction items, but no polysomnography macroarchitecture, EEG spectral power, or odds ratio product sleep-depth measure was associated with daily dysfunction after multiple-comparison correction. Suggests whole-night PSG averages may not fully capture daily dysfunction.

papers.title: Slow power-envelope associations among brain, heart, and gut signals during sleep: an exploratory multivariate transfer entropy study.
papers.summary: Applied multivariate transfer entropy to overnight occipital EEG, ECG, and bowel sound signals from 24 healthy subjects to quantify directed slow power-envelope associations among brain, heart, and gut across sleep stages. Information flow from heart to brain, brain to gut, and heart to gut consistently exceeded reverse directions, with stage-dependent inter-system patterns such as suppressed heart-to-gut and brain-to-gut flow in deep sleep.

papers.title: Temporal Associations Between Physiological Sleep and Next-Day Pain Intensity in Individuals With Activity-Limiting Chronic Pain: A Multiple Night At-Home Ear-EEG Sleep-Monitoring Study.
papers.summary: Pre-registered prospective observational study using at-home ear-EEG across 11-33 nights in 19 individuals with chronic pain found that lower next-day pain intensity was associated with greater duration, percentage and stability of N3 sleep, while higher next-day pain was associated with N3 fragmentation and higher N1 proportion. Demonstrates within-person night-to-night sleep-pain associations via physiological monitoring.

papers.title: The Role of Drosophila Toll Receptors in the Central Nervous System.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on the nine Drosophila Toll receptors (Toll-1 to Toll-9), describing non-canonical signaling roles in the CNS including axon guidance, synaptic partner matching, neuronal survival versus apoptosis via dMyD88/Sarm adaptor recruitment, adult brain plasticity, sleep homeostasis, and neuro-immune interactions relevant to neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Dynamics of Sleep Architecture and Nocturnal Oxygen Saturation During Acclimatization at Intermediate Altitude: A Longitudinal Observational Study in Elite Athletes.
papers.summary: In 17 elite mogul-ski athletes undergoing a 2-week camp at 2100 m, wearable EEG-oximetry showed total sleep time was unchanged but %N3 declined and %REM rose logarithmically across the first week, while SpO2 was lower and overnight heart rate higher than in normoxia, with SpO2 recovery occurring fastest in N1 and REM and slowest in N2/N3. The authors conclude that acclimatization dynamics are sleep-stage-specific and that the first two nights capture the most rapid adjustments.

papers.title: Poststroke sleep phenotypes and executive dysfunction: toward a sleep-network-executive framework.
papers.summary: This targeted synthesis of clinical stroke, neuroimaging, non-stroke sleep-network, and intervention evidence proposes a sleep-network-executive framework in which sleep fragmentation, insomnia, and arousal instability act as functional stressors on vulnerable post-stroke salience, default mode, and frontoparietal networks, impairing executive function; no study has directly tested the complete pathway, so the framework is presented as a falsifiable mechanistic hypothesis.

papers.title: Poor Test-Retest Stability of Nocturnal REM Sleep Onset Markers in Narcolepsy Type 1.
papers.summary: In 227 untreated children and adults with narcolepsy type 1 who underwent two overnight polysomnograms, nocturnal sleep-onset REM periods (nSOREMPs) showed poor test-retest agreement (κ=0.26), present on both nights in only 41.8%, and nocturnal direct REM transitions were similarly unstable; persistence was associated with younger age, shorter MSLT sleep latency, and lower CSF hypocretin-1, suggesting variable REM dysregulation rather than a stable trait.

papers.title: Affective burden and resting-state EEG microstate dynamics in sleep-severity-matched chronic insomnia.
papers.summary: In 21 pairs of treatment-naive chronic insomnia patients matched on subjective sleep severity, the high-affective-burden phenotype showed greater EEG microstate C coverage and lower microstate D coverage, occurrence, and duration during eyes-open rest, with a four-feature classifier reaching cross-validated AUC 74.8%.

papers.title: CLEC1B and RAC1 in peripheral immune remodeling associated with sleep disturbance: an exploratory integrative study.
papers.summary: Integrating blood eQTL and GWAS data with mouse and human PBMC transcriptomics and single-cell data, this exploratory study nominated CLEC1B and RAC1 as candidate genes linked to peripheral B-cell remodeling under sleep disturbance, with lower Rac1 mRNA (P=0.017) and lower CLEC1B (P=0.0056) and RAC1 (P=0.0016) protein in sleep-deprived mouse PBMCs.

papers.title: Tryptophan metabolism circadian regulation: clinical and pharmacological implications.
papers.summary: This review discusses the bidirectional relationship between the circadian clock and tryptophan metabolism through the kynurenine, serotonin-melatonin, and microbiota-derived indole-AhR pathways, emphasizing time-of-day variation in metabolites as biomarkers and proposing pharmacological targeting of tryptophan pathways or use of tryptophan derivatives as a circadian medicine approach.

papers.title: Feedback Valence, Prediction Error, and the Limits of Computational Attribution in Symptom-Related EEG
papers.summary: Reanalyzing two open probabilistic-learning EEG datasets, the authors reproduced a trait-anxiety-related FCz feedback contrast (larger negative-minus-positive theta response after depression adjustment) but found feedback valence and signed prediction error nearly collinear (r=-0.964) and showed that population-level model discrimination can succeed despite poor participant-level recovery of neural slopes, limiting theta-specific and computational attribution.

papers.title: Distinct Systemic Metabolic Remodeling and Neurobehavioral Deterioration in Chemotherapy-Treated Lung Cancer Models.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Comparing chemotherapy-treated subcutaneous and orthotopic Lewis lung carcinoma mouse models, the authors found divergent survival and neurobehavioral trajectories, with orthotopic tumors showing greater systemic deterioration and broader plasma metabolic remodeling (ketone body, glutathione, one-carbon, redox pathways). Both models showed peripheral oxidative stress and brain changes involving Claudin-5, glial activation, and synaptic markers.

papers.title: A single day of natural daylight exposure and physical activity does not conclusively change circadian phase: A Bayesian crossover experiment
papers.summary: In a Bayesian crossover experiment with 41 healthy adults, a single 8-h natural daylight exposure with or without ~4 h hiking did not conclusively shift circadian phase, with estimated DLMO changes of -4.22 min per SD increase in illuminance and -6.48 min per SD increase in heart rate reserve. Exploratory sleepiness, mood, wellbeing, exertion, and vigilance outcomes were largely inconclusive or negligible.

papers.title: Multi-night evaluation of the Oura Ring in free-living older adults: App-reported sleep efficiency as an indicator of measurement stability.
papers.summary: Evaluated Oura Ring Gen3 sleep metrics against the Dreem 3 EEG headband over 210 paired free-living nights in 45 older adults, finding moderate sleep/wake agreement (accuracy 85.3%) with Oura underestimating TST, SE, and REM and overestimating SOL. Participants with lower Oura-determined sleep efficiency (<85%) showed larger TST bias, poorer agreement, and greater night-to-night bias variability, suggesting SE as a context indicator of measurement stability.

papers.title: Cannabidiol and fronto-parietal EEG connectivity in autistic children.
papers.summary: In a double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial, resting-state EEG from autistic children (n=18 analyzed) showed increased beta-band right fronto-parietal (F4-P8) functional connectivity after 12 weeks of oral cannabidiol versus placebo, with no significant placebo-period changes. The authors present this as preliminary evidence requiring replication in larger samples.

papers.title: Rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder as a model of early neurodegeneration: challenges for research and clinical diagnosis.
papers.summary: Reviews REM sleep behavior disorder (loss of REM atonia with dream enactment) as a clinically accessible model and marker of prodromal α-synucleinopathy neurodegeneration, driven by dysfunction in distributed brainstem REM regulatory networks. Argues for a broader framework integrating polysomnography with multimodal biomarkers and network-based models to improve risk stratification, prognosis, and early intervention.

papers.title: Tick tock: how the body's circadian clock keeps cardiometabolic rhythm in check.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes mechanistic roles of core circadian clock genes and central and peripheral clocks in cardiometabolic health, describing how chronodisruption from shift work, irregular sleep, artificial light at night, and erratic eating promotes hormonal dysregulation, inflammation, and metabolic impairment. It discusses pharmacological clock modulation and personalized chronotherapy as emerging strategies.

papers.title: Information leakage and performance overestimation in EEG-based schizophrenia detection: evidence from literature and empirical analyses.
papers.summary: Reviews EEG-based schizophrenia detection literature, finding ~65% of published works use erroneous evaluation practices (e.g., epoch-level splitting, feature selection before partitioning), and empirically shows on three open datasets that such information leakage can inflate classification accuracy by up to ~30%. Calls for establishing leakage-free best practices before clinical deployment.

papers.title: Comparison between Three-Night and Single-Night Actigraphic Sleep Assessment During Early Hospitalization.
papers.summary: In a multicenter cross-sectional study of 64 inpatients monitored by wrist actigraphy over the first three hospital nights, single-night values approximated 3-night averages for actual sleep time, mobile time, sleep efficiency, fragmentation index, and light exposure (ICC ≈ 0.71-0.75) with no systematic bias, whereas sleep latency was less reliable (ICC = 0.51). Rest-activity rhythm was fragmented despite preserved relative amplitude.

papers.title: Augmented cardiac growth hormone signaling in circadian-disrupted cardiomyopathy.
papers.summary: This minireview proposes that the cardiac growth hormone axis mediates circadian-disruption-induced cardiomyopathy, suggesting the cardiomyocyte molecular clock, plausibly via REV-ERBα, restricts GH responsiveness and that mistimed GH signaling promotes hypertrophy, fibrosis, and metabolic inflexibility. It cites cardiomyocyte-specific Bmal1-deficient mice showing increased GH-induced STAT5 phosphorylation, Igf1 expression, and remodeling partially attenuated by reduced GH receptor dosage.

papers.title: Evaluating the frequency of conspecific pecking and foraging behaviors in two genetic strains of turkey toms with or without environmental enrichment.
papers.summary: Tested a hanging jute rope enrichment in 1,056 turkey toms from two Large White strains and found the rope did not affect conspecific pecking, foraging, production metrics, mortality, or pecking-related culls. Strain A showed heavier body weight, faster gain, higher feed intake, and more head/neck and rope pecking than strain B, with more back/wing/tail pecking and foraging in the afternoon at 4 weeks.

papers.title: Participant-Disjoint EEG Decoding of Instructed Respiratory Conditions Using a Deep Spatio-Respiratory Transformer.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: The authors developed a Deep Spatio-Respiratory Transformer (DSRT) for participant-disjoint EEG decoding of eight instructed respiratory conditions, combining differential entropy and normalized power-ratio features with squeeze-and-excitation recalibration, a four-layer Transformer encoder, and nasal/oral pathway supervision. At the participant level it reached 0.7429 ± 0.0492 accuracy, improving on EEG Conformer by about 3.8 percentage points in accuracy and Macro-F1 with 1.297M parameters and 3.825 ms median latency.

papers.title: Altered Melatonin Secretion and Recurrent Sleep-Related Headache in a Patient With a Pineal Cyst: A Case Report.
papers.summary: Case report of a 23-year-old woman with strictly nocturnal (1:30-4:00 a.m.) stereotyped headaches and a benign pineal cyst, who had reduced 3:00 a.m. melatonin (14 and 16 pg/mL vs. 40-80 reference). Oral melatonin (4 mg, then 8 mg nightly) produced complete headache resolution by six weeks, with normalized nocturnal melatonin (52 pg/mL) and no recurrence at six months.

papers.title: Environmental enrichment is associated with changes in the gut microbiome and resistome of captive pythons.
papers.summary: Using shotgun metagenomic sequencing of Burmese and reticulated pythons before and after environmental enrichment, the authors report host-dependent shifts in gut microbiome composition, with increased alpha-diversity and carbohydrate metabolism potential in Burmese pythons. Pseudomonadota contributed most antibiotic resistance genes, indicating enrichment-associated changes in the gut resistome.

papers.title: Integrating uncertainty and practice variability for epilepsy prognostication after intracranial EEG: A meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This meta-analysis of 115 studies found that 67% of drug-resistant epilepsy patients undergoing intracranial EEG proceeded to resection, with 52% achieving seizure freedom and 58% favorable outcomes. Individual patient-level modeling identified lesional MRI and cortical malformation as predictors of favorable outcome, and bilateral implantation as a predictor of less favorable outcome, though discrimination was modest.

papers.title: Tian Wang Bu Xin Dan Attenuates Neuronal Injury in LPS-Treated HT22 Cells and PCPA-Induced Insomnia-Model Rats.
papers.summary: A cinnabar-free modified Tian Wang Bu Xin Dan extract was profiled by LC-MS and network analysis, then tested in LPS-treated HT22 cells and PCPA-induced insomnia rats, where it shifted PI3K/AKT, autophagy (Beclin 1, LC3-II/LC3-I, p62), inflammation, and apoptosis markers toward control levels and improved sleep responses, anxiety-like behavior, spatial learning, and hippocampal CA1 injury.

papers.title: Multiscale Neurodynamic Alterations in Major Depressive Disorder Revealed by Lempel-Ziv Complexity of Multi-Paradigm Resting-State EEG.
papers.summary: Using multiscale Lempel-Ziv complexity on resting-state EEG across eyes-open and eyes-closed paradigms, the study found impaired complexity transitions from low to high frequencies and disrupted delta-centered cross-scale integration in MDD patients versus controls, with classification models reaching up to 85.71% accuracy.

papers.title: Harnessing Neuroendocrine and Circadian Clocks in Beneficial Insects for Agricultural Chrono-Management.
papers.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on how circadian clocks, hormones, and biogenic amines regulate behavior and life-history development in beneficial insects such as pollinators and natural enemies. It proposes an 'agricultural chrono-management' framework using environmental cues to align insect activity with farming schedules, while noting most evidence remains laboratory-based with limited field validation.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Graph Analysis Reveals Enhanced Alpha-Band Integration in High-IQ Individuals: The MENSA-Connect Project.
papers.summary: Resting-state 64-channel EEG with Lagged Linear Coherence and graph-theory analysis in 29 MENSA members versus 20 controls showed lower alpha-band characteristic path length (greater global integration) and higher beta-band clustering coefficient with higher path length (greater local specialization) in high-IQ individuals, with no small-worldness differences.

papers.title: Personalized Postoperative Pain Management and Therapies Based on Pharmacogenomics.
papers.summary: This narrative review proposes a staged precision-medicine framework for postoperative pain management that separates clinically actionable pharmacogenomics (notably CYP2D6-guided codeine and tramadol prescribing) from heterogeneous risk modifiers and investigational adjuncts. It characterizes dopamine-related pathways, Reward Deficiency Syndrome constructs, and Continuous Visual Attention Test measures as exploratory rather than validated prescribing tools.

papers.title: Physiological insights and clinical evidence of high flow nasal cannula as first-line therapy for acute hypercapnic exacerbation of COPD: a narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review of 17 studies assessed high flow nasal cannula (HFNC) as first-line therapy in hypercapnic acute exacerbation of COPD, finding HFNC often associated with better comfort and tolerance than conventional oxygen therapy or non-invasive ventilation. Compared with conventional oxygen therapy, HFNC might reduce treatment failure, and compared with NIV it had similar effects on dyspnoea and blood gas analysis, though evidence on treatment failure remains uncertain.

papers.title: Tetramelic Monodactyly With Neonatal Encephalopathy: A Case Report.
papers.summary: A case report of a neonate with tetramelic monodactyly and neonatal encephalopathy in whom rapid trio whole-genome sequencing identified a pathogenic 10q24.31q24.32 duplication, a locus previously associated with split-hand/foot malformation. The variant segregated with limb anomalies in the father and older sister, suggesting an autosomal dominant pattern.

papers.title: Tirzepatide for the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea: from apnea-hypopnea index reduction to cardiometabolic risk mitigation-a narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review evaluates tirzepatide, the first FDA-approved pharmacotherapy for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity, anchoring evidence in the SURMOUNT-OSA trial program. In SURMOUNT-OSA, tirzepatide produced randomized, placebo-controlled reductions in apnea-hypopnea index, sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, body weight, and systemic inflammation, though cardiovascular, renal, and mortality signals derive only from nonrandomized observational cohorts and remain exploratory.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
